target_customer: Restaurant chains and food businesses (paid alerts, benchmarking, API), plus public health agencies and consumers who use it free
problem: Foodborne illness outbreaks are detected late because victims rarely report and brands learn too late. Dinesafe collects consumer food poisoning reports, geo-analyzes them in real time and alerts businesses and health agencies.
business_model: B2B subscriptions (alerts, benchmarks, API, certification) built on a free consumer report site; later government data contract
product_category: Food safety surveillance and crowdsourced reporting

founders.name: Patrick Quade
founders.background_notes: Bloomberg headline listed on the YC page calls him an ex-banker, text not opened. Started Iwaspoisoned.com after food poisoning from a Tribeca deli per his Launch HN post. Education not found.

competitors.name: Yelp user reviews as an informal illness signal
competitors.what: Restaurant reviews that mention food poisoning, studied by health departments for outbreak detection

technical_complexity.rationale: A moderated web form, geo clustering and alerting are standard web engineering. Fraud filtering is the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: A decade of iwaspoisoned.com reports, 350+ health agencies self-reported in 2018 and restaurant relationships are hard to replicate quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying it. The FDA reportedly became a data partner in 2021 per a directory listing.

market_need_then: The 2017 Chipotle outbreaks drew press about crowdsourced illness reports (Bloomberg July 2017, NPR Nov 2017, per the YC page), and a 2017 JMIR study found reports preceded official confirmation in several outbreaks.

branding.domain_note: Uses dinesafe.org, a .org rather than .com. Same name is used by Toronto's restaurant inspection program, per the trademark search.
branding.brand_signature: Dinesafe Certification for well ranked restaurant brands
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage by Bloomberg, NPR and the New York Times on the crowdsourcing idea, not the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name shared with Toronto's DineSafe inspection program and other trademarks. The older iwaspoisoned.com name carried the consumer recognition.

outcome_analysis: Dinesafe is a tiny team of about six that grew out of the iwaspoisoned.com report site, joined YC in summer 2018 and sells to restaurant chains and public health. No equity funding beyond an unverified small seed was found. A directory says the FDA awarded a contract in 2021. It is active but small, with a niche market and no public traction after 2019.
notes: Seed of about 120K reported only by aggregators (CB Insights July 2018, Persana September 2018), not recorded as a round. dinesafe.org fetch returned no content. The Yelp entry is an informal substitute signal, not a funded direct competitor, and no named direct competitor was found dated near the batch. Traction figures are self-reported on Launch HN. The Launch HN copy is a blog mirror. Completeness pass: Recorded the $120K seed; dated 2018-07 by CB Insights and 2018-09 by Prospeo and Persana, so only the year is kept. The recorded round rests on a single database or outlet and was not cross-checked by press.
